name: Perioperative Risk Stratification, Monitoring, and Surgical Complications

reference.source: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22nd ed / ACC-AHA Guidelines
clinicalPearls: The Revised Cardiac Risk Index (Lee criteria) predicts major adverse cardiac events before non-cardiac surgery
Postoperative fever causes follow the classic timeline: atelectasis (24-48h), UTI (day 3), SSI (day 5-7), and DVT/PE (day 7+)
Malignant hyperthermia triggered by volatile anesthetics or succinylcholine requires immediate cessation and IV dantrolene (2.5 mg/kg)
Clavien-Dindo classification grades surgical complications from Grade I (minor deviation) to Grade V (death)
Smoking cessation should occur at least 4 to 8 weeks before elective surgery to significantly reduce postoperative pulmonary complications
reference.pathophysiology: Surgical trauma and anesthetic agents disrupt physiological homeostasis through neuroendocrine activation, fluid third-spacing, and immunosuppression. Atelectasis results from loss of functional residual capacity and surfactant inactivation during general anesthesia. Surgical site infections arise from bacterial contamination of the operative field exceeding 10^5 organisms per gram of tissue. Malignant hyperthermia results from an autosomal dominant RYR1 gene mutation causing uncontrolled calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum into skeletal myocytes, provoking hypermetabolism, muscle rigidity, and lethal rhabdomyolysis.
additionalDifferentials: Postoperative pulmonary atelectasis versus aspiration pneumonitis
Surgical site hematoma versus superficial incisional infection
Prerenal azotemia versus acute tubular necrosis after major blood loss
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome versus malignant hyperthermia
additionalInvestigations: Twelve-lead ECG and functional capacity assessment (METs) for cardiac risk stratification
Complete blood count, serum creatinine, and electrolytes
Duplex ultrasound of lower extremities for suspected deep vein thrombosis
Computed tomography of surgical bed for suspected deep intra-abdominal collection
